Gradient boosting offers a flexible, interpretable model for game outcome prediction. Player-level QB tracking introduces granular performance signals that improve model discrimination. Dualities emerge between ensemble methods and sequential learning, where Kalman updates refine predictions iteratively while boosting captures non-linear dependencies. Failure modes include overfitting in gradient boosting, stale ratings in Kalman filters, and misalignment in player tracking due to data latency or incomplete transitions.
